executive_summary:
President Trump issued a proclamation directing negotiations with trading partners to adjust imports of robotics and industrial machinery, following a Commerce Department finding that these imports threaten U.S. national security [1](https://www.unite.ai/trump-directs-robotics-import-talks-after-commerce-security-finding/). The Federal Communications Commission is scheduled to vote on a rule change allowing drones to operate on cell networks [2](https://seekingalpha.com/instablog/39580-michael-a-gayed-cfa/6355186-the-fcc-is-about-to-put-drones-on-cell-networks-wall-street-is-selling-the-networks). NASA’s Quesst mission completed 40 additional flights of the X-59 quiet supersonic research aircraft, reaching speeds up to Mach 1.53 [3](https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/quesst/2026/10/28/nasa-celebrates-a-year-of-progress-since-first-x-59-flight/).

DTL Transport will operate 75 driverless trucks equipped with the Kodiak Driver autonomous system on routes in the Sun Belt [4](https://www.automotiveworld.com/news/dtl-transport-to-run-75-driverless-trucks-with-kodiak-ai/). A Seoul court rejected a lawsuit by 88 Tesla owners seeking refunds for Full Self-Driving software, ruling that the carmaker did not breach contractual obligations [5](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/3372513/tesla-owners-south-korea-lose-legal-battle-over-full-self-driving-promises). The Ministry of Science and ICT and ETRI revised the international standard SAE J3016, which classifies autonomous driving into six stages [6](https://www.mt.co.kr/en/tech/2026/10/29/2026102909515047023). SkyDrive welcomed a U.S. principal officer to discuss commercial eVTOL deployment and bilateral cooperation between Japan and the United States [7](https://skydrive.co.jp/en/news/73181/).

Transmashholding completed assembly of a hydrogen fuel cell powered passenger trainset for operation on Sakhalin, with testing scheduled to begin in November [8](https://www.railwaygazette.com/hydrogen/2026/10/28/transmashholding-completes-hydrogen-train-ahead-of-sakhalin-trials/). The Africa Finance Corporation selected preferred bidders for civil works sections of the Zambia Lobito Railway [9](https://www.railway.supply/zambia-angola-rail-civil-works-bidders-named-rolling-stock-lot-unaddressed/). The U.S. military anticipates spending $1.1 billion to purchase roughly 300,000 drones, with rules implemented to eliminate Chinese components from its drone systems [10](https://tuzarapost.substack.com/p/the-us-militarys-1-billion-drone).

Spain began three days of mourning after a high-speed rail collision in Castilla-La Mancha killed 68 people [11](https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/spain-mourns-latest-train-tragedy-015317589.html). Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported intercepting and destroying an MQ-1 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz [12](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-s-army-says-it-downed-mq-1-drone-east-of-strait-of-hormuz/4104525). Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin stated that more than 600 drones attacked the city overnight, with Russian air defenses shooting down most of them [13](https://kuwaittimes.com/article/52619/world/moscow-hit-by-more-than-600-drones-overnight-mayor-says/). Embassy in Riyadh warned of potential attacks on airports and travel disruptions in Saudi Arabia, citing recent missile and drone attacks by Iran-backed Houthis [14](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610283763).
what_to_watch: The outcome of the US-Iran diplomatic outreach, including whether the letter from Vice President Vance to Iran's security chief leads to a resumption of peace talks or further escalation in the Strait of Hormuz.

The operational rollout of the DTL Transport and Kodiak AI partnership, specifically the deployment of the first 75 driverless trucks and the practical application of the per-mile fee model for interstate long-haul freight.

The investigation and safety review following the second high-speed rail disaster in Spain in nine months, and its potential impact on the country's upcoming general election and national rail safety standards.

UAS / Drones.title: The FCC Is About to Put Drones on Cell Networks. Wall Street Is Selling the Networks.
UAS / Drones.summary: Originally published at The Free Markets Report, a free daily on deregulation and markets. Tomorrow morning the Federal Communications Commission votes on a one-paragraph change to a 1991 rule.

Counter-UAS / Airspace Security.title: Counter-Drone Systems Explained: How They Work and Cost
Counter-UAS / Airspace Security.summary: RTX announced on October 13 that it was awarded $729 million for components of the Low, slow, small unmanned aircraft Integrated Defeat System (LIDS) for the US Army, Qatar, and Jordan. The Department of Homeland Security announced in early August a five-year contract vehicle with a $1.5 billion ceiling and 12 awardees.

AAM / eVTOL / Advanced Aviation.title: SkyDrive Welcomes U.S. Principal Officer Anna Wang to Advance Bilateral Cooperation on Commercial eVTOL Deployment
AAM / eVTOL / Advanced Aviation.summary: On Oct. 23, SkyDrive welcomed Anna Wang, principal officer of the U.S. Consulate Nagoya, to its Nagoya Airport office to discuss the commercialization of eVTOL aircraft and bilateral cooperation between Japan and the United States. Principal Officer Wang expressed support for facilitating coordination with relevant agencies to accelerate deployment and promoting business initiatives in the United States.

Autonomous Vehicles.title: DTL Transport to run 75 driverless trucks with Kodiak AI
Autonomous Vehicles.summary: DTL Transport will run 75 driverless trucks fitted with the Kodiak Driver autonomous system, paying Kodiak AI a per-mile fee for its use. Service starts in the Sun Belt on two lanes: I-10 from Dallas to El Paso and I-20 from Dallas to Atlanta.

Autonomous Vehicles.title: Tesla owners in South Korea lose legal battle over full self-driving promises
Autonomous Vehicles.summary: A Seoul court on Thursday rejected a lawsuit by 88 Tesla owners seeking full refunds for Full Self-Driving (FSD) software, ruling that the carmaker had not breached its contractual obligations. The Seoul Central District Court found that the FSD option did not promise fully autonomous driving without human intervention and that Tesla had already provided some of the functions included in the package.

Autonomous Vehicles.title: International autonomous driving standard revised, led by South Korea… to be applied worldwide
Autonomous Vehicles.summary: The Ministry of Science and ICT and ETRI revised the international standard 'SAE J3016,' which classifies autonomous driving into six stages from 'Level 0' to 'Level 5.' The 2026 revised edition was officially published on the 20th of last month and will be applied by companies and institutional investors worldwide.

Robotics.title: Trump Directs Robotics Import Talks After Commerce Security Finding
Robotics.summary: President Donald J. Trump issued a proclamation on October 28, 2026, concurring with a Commerce Department finding that imports of robotics, industrial machinery, and their parts and components threaten to impair U.S. national security, and directing negotiations with trading partners to adjust those imports.

Robotics.title: Sensors, Software and Motion: Chongqing Builds Its Robotics Plans Around Vehicle Technology
Robotics.summary: Chongqing plans to expand robotics development from 2026 to 2030, aiming to raise the industry's output value to more than 100 billion yuan by building on shared technological foundations with its automotive sector.

Robotics.title: Interview with Faraday Future chairman: Moving from Chinese robot sourcing to US manufacturing
Robotics.summary: Faraday Future plans to bring a US robot factory online by the end of 2026, with its first US-assembled robot scheduled for February 2027. The company aims to introduce three to five new or next-generation robotics products in the country each year while developing domestic suppliers and manufacturing capabilities.

Robotics.title: Audi Testing Humanoid Robots for Logistics
Robotics.summary: Audi has begun testing humanoid robots to automate parts sequencing at its Ingolstadt plant, where workers make some 1 million picks daily. The project involves Agile Robots supplying the humanoids, NVIDIA providing artificial intelligence software, and Dassault Systèmes supplying simulation software to create a virtual twin for testing feasibility, timings, ergonomics, and safety.

Civil Supersonics / High-Speed Aviation.title: NASA Celebrates a Year of Progress Since First X-59 Flight
Civil Supersonics / High-Speed Aviation.summary: NASA's Quesst mission completed 40 additional flights of the X-59 quiet supersonic research aircraft since its first flight on Oct. 28, 2025, reaching a maximum altitude of more than 56,000 feet and speeds up to Mach 1.53.

Advanced Rail / High-Speed Rail.title: Spain mourns after latest train tragedy kills 68
Advanced Rail / High-Speed Rail.summary: Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after a high-speed rail collision in Castilla-La Mancha killed 68 people and injured scores. Transport Minister Oscar Puente reported an "error" and "inexplicable circumstances" when the control centre decided to resume traffic despite an automatic control system failure.

Advanced Rail / High-Speed Rail.title: Urban rail industry news round-up
Advanced Rail / High-Speed Rail.summary: Roscosmos company UKVZ delivered a 1 435 mm gauge Type 71-623 tram for testing in Rostov-on-Don, while CRRC Changchun Railway Vehicles unveiled the first of 10 five-car trainsets for Buenos Aires metro lines A and C.

Advanced Rail / High-Speed Rail.title: Zambia–Angola rail civil works bidders named, rolling stock lot unaddressed
Advanced Rail / High-Speed Rail.summary: Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) has chosen preferred bidders for both civil works sections of the Zambia Lobito Railway, an 830-km greenfield line linking Chingola in Zambia with Luacano in Angola. In Zambia, the preferred bidder is a consortium led by Webuild S.p.A., with Mota-Engil and IC İçtaş Construction as partners.

Advanced Rail / High-Speed Rail.title: Transmashholding completes hydrogen train ahead of Sakhalin trials
Advanced Rail / High-Speed Rail.summary: Transmashholding’s Demikhovo factory has completed assembly of a hydrogen fuel cell powered passenger trainset for operation on the island of Sakhalin, and work is underway on a second. Testing of the first trainset is scheduled to begin in November followed by certification trials in 2027.

Military UAS.title: Iran’s army says it downed MQ-1 drone east of Strait of Hormuz
Military UAS.summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) intercepted and destroyed an MQ-1 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz, the semi-official ISNA news agency reported Thursday, citing the force.

Military UAS.title: Moscow hit by more than 600 drones overnight, mayor says
Military UAS.summary: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 600 drones attacked the city and surrounding region overnight, with Russian air defenses shooting down most of them. Russian media reported temporary flight restrictions at Domodedovo, Vnukovo, and Zhukovsky airports, which were lifted shortly before 7:00 am local time.

International Security.title: The US Military’s $1 Billion Drone Plan to Take on China — and How They Hope They Never Have to Use Them
International Security.summary: The U.S. military anticipates spending $1.1 billion to purchase roughly 300,000 drones from Gauntlet exercises, with the goal of eventually selecting two to four companies to mass produce small drones. The department has implemented rules to eliminate Chinese components, such as brushless motors and battery packs, from its drone systems.

International Security.title: US warns of Iran-backed Houthi attacks, travel disruptions in Saudi Arabia | Iran International
International Security.summary: The US Embassy in Riyadh warned of potential attacks on airports and travel disruptions in Saudi Arabia, citing recent missile and drone attacks by Iran-backed Houthis. The embassy said the State Department had ordered non-emergency US government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia effective October 23 due to safety risks.

International Security.title: Canadian volunteer who rescued hundreds of animals is killed in Russian drone strike in Donetsk Oblast
International Security.summary: Canadian volunteer Jesse Adams, who rescued animals and helped people in Ukraine, has been killed by a Russian drone strike while evacuating animals in Donetsk Oblast. On 25 October, his vehicle was struck by a Russian FPV drone, leaving him with severe injuries that doctors were unable to save.
